payload.claim: In `_export_from_volume`, `head_sha` is computed (line 987) and `patch.diff` is written to `task_dir` (line 989) before `patch.json` is built, which calls `worktree.changed_files(target, spec.tree_base)` (line 996). If that last read fails (e.g. the ephemeral container's fourth git call errors after the first three succeeded), control falls into the `except Exception as exc:` at line 1008, which reports `export_failed` and returns `(None, subjects)` — discarding the already-computed `head_sha` even though a real, complete `patch.diff` is now sitting in `task_dir` with no matching `patch.json`. The caller (and anything reading the returned head sha) is told the export produced nothing, while a usable patch file is actually on disk unreferenced by any success signal. The equivalent base-path failure (lines 1086-1111) at least preserves the already-assigned `head_sha` across the exception because that variable is shared with the outer function scope; the volume path's local `head_sha` is not, making this an avoidable loss of an already-exported artifact's identity in exactly the failure-recovery path this change exists to add.
